decks.name: LeetCode #57 - Insert Interval
decks.description: Insert and merge a new interval into sorted non-overlapping intervals

cards.question: Insert Interval: You are given an array of non-overlapping intervals intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi] represent the start and the end of the ith interval and intervals is sorted in ascending order by starti. You are also given an interval newInterval = [start, end] that represents the start and end of another interval. Insert newInterval into intervals such that intervals is still sorted in ascending order by starti and intervals still does not have any overlapping intervals (merge overlapping intervals if necessary). Return intervals after the insertion.

solutions.name: Linear Search
solutions.explanation: Use three-phase linear scan to insert and merge interval. Phase 1: Add all intervals that end before newInterval starts (no overlap). Phase 2: Merge all intervals that overlap with newInterval by expanding newInterval's boundaries to include them. Phase 3: Add remaining intervals after newInterval. Single pass through array handles all cases. O(n) time with simple logic. Most straightforward approach.

solutions.name: Binary Search
solutions.explanation: Optimize insertion position finding with binary search. First handle empty intervals edge case. Use binary search to find correct position to insert newInterval based on start times. Insert newInterval at found position. Then merge all overlapping intervals in single pass: if current interval doesn't overlap with last in result, add it; otherwise merge by extending last interval's end. Binary search reduces position finding from O(n) to O(log n) but overall still O(n) due to insertion and merging.

solutions.name: Greedy
solutions.explanation: Single-pass greedy approach with three distinct cases. For each interval, check: (1) if newInterval ends before current interval starts, append newInterval and return with remaining intervals (done early); (2) if newInterval starts after current interval ends, append current interval (no overlap); (3) if they overlap, merge by updating newInterval boundaries to include current interval. After loop, append final newInterval. Most elegant solution with early termination optimization. O(n) time with best average case performance.
